task_instance: Run the github-triage workflow's Phase 0/1 (select target repo via `gh auth status` + `git remote -v`, then `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` / `gh pr list --state merged`) against a real GitHub-hosted repository, as the minimal representative slice of the skill's core deliverable (triaging live open issues/PRs, including proposing closes/cross-links/merges that require gh write access).
blocker_detail: The skill's entire workflow is built on the `gh` CLI operating against a real, authenticated GitHub account/repo: Phase 0 starts with `gh auth status` to confirm auth, Phase 1 pulls live issue/PR JSON via `gh issue list`/`gh pr list`, and Phases 2/5 require `gh pr merge`, `gh issue close`, `gh issue comment`, `gh pr edit` (real writes to GitHub). In this runtime, `gh auth status` reports the configured GH_TOKEN is invalid ('Failed to log in to github.com using token (GH_TOKEN)... The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid.'), so there is no working GitHub account/session to read real issue/PR data from, let alone write to. My task's safety rules additionally forbid using or searching for credentials/tokens, forbid account-bound services, and forbid any writes to external services (merges, issue closes, comments) -- so even if a valid token were available, the write half of the skill (Phase 2 merges, Phase 5 closes/comments/cross-links) could not be exercised regardless. There is no local/offline substitute for 'triage a repository's open GitHub issues and PRs via the gh CLI' -- it inherently requires a live, authenticated GitHub API session against a hosted repo, which this runtime does not provide and which I am barred from provisioning.
evidence: Ran `gh auth status` in the work directory: output was 'github.com / X Failed to log in to github.com using token (GH_TOKEN) / - Active account: true / - The token in GH_TOKEN is invalid.' `which gh` confirmed the CLI binary exists at /usr/local/bin/gh, so the blocker is authentication/account state, not a missing tool. Per the task's Safety Rules I did not attempt to search for, install, or substitute credentials, and did not call the GitHub MCP tool as a workaround. No further skill phases (issue/PR listing, classification, scoring, or any gated writes) could be attempted without a working GitHub session, and the write phases are separately forbidden by the safety rules ('no ... issues, comments or any other writes to external services'). Stopped at this point per instruction 4 ('If the task inherently needs any of these, stop at that point and record it as the blocker. Do not work around it.').
